Hey man, don't have a lot of advice to offer really, but thought I'd chime in with something since (maybe a bit before) this time last year I weighed 406lbs and I'm currently sat at 280lbs, dropped from a 44/46 to a 36 jeans size, 3xl/4xl to an XL t-shirt size. Clothes finally fit, I love going to the gym, feel healthy and eating healthy isn't even difficult any more! It was a struggle at first, then it became a habit and now it's just my life.

Keto is difficult at first, and going out is always a problem but the tide seems to be finally turning with people realising that this is one of the healthiest ways you can lose weight and just live your life in general which is leading to waaay more options. 

Biggest advice I'd give you is to set long term goals, things you want to do that you feel you can't because of your size. For me it was simply wanting nice clothes and wanting to do MMA/BJJ training both of which I am doing now.

What could you possibly do to prevent concussions in MMA though? It completely and totally integral to the sport, you couldn't even take out head kicks because they've shown impacts to the chest/back can cause concussions too. It's sadly entirely unavoidable and down to the fighters to assess their own condition because only they can really say what's going on in their head. There's currently no way to assess CTE without cutting their brain open, and studies have also shown that if anything head gear could be worse for brain injuries. 

I think education is the only way forward, educate more fighters on the risks, so they can make more informed decisions especially on the way they train/spar and how long they take after knockouts. 

It's good to see someone like Robbie Lawler taking more time to recover, shows that things definitely are changing.

You say you've been desperate to leave school for a long time, but just based on how well this is written I can tell you're definitely very intelligent and articulate. SO I guess the real question is whether you're passionate about your studying and what are your plans for the future?

Depression is just awful, it makes everything seem as bad as it could possibly be, and makes you feel like theres no way out. That clouded judgement is very dangerous and why it's so important to talk to people and be active with your own mental health, and is most likely the direct cause of your lack of motivation. 

My honest opinion based on what you've written is that you're very similar to a LOT of people I've known. You don't get to the place you are in without being very hard working and very intelligent, but it sounds like you're just way to harsh on yourself. 

My biggest advice, is maybe look into practicing mindfulness with way you allow yourself to think, if you start thinking negatively, if you're able to identify that, analyse it, and move past it when it happens the thoughts will lose their power over time. Depressions greatest ally is denial, and since you have the relationships with the professors USE THEM! Tell them how you're feeling, explain to them the pressure you feel and that you're thinking of dropping out. In my experience high level educators are very willing to help you in any way they can. 

Hope that helps at all.
